components.criterion: The view reads from below the standing subject rather than eye-level or above, through the underside of the chin and overhead bench/roof geometry.
Upward-facing projection includes overhead roof ribs and a clear view of architectural undersides.
Nearby boots/lower body are visibly enlarged relative to the receding upper body/head in the same connected subject.
Multiple vertical iron columns recede and converge toward the upper frame; this is coherent spatial perspective, not isolated leaning props.

confusion_boundaries: A Dutch roll or diagonal frame alone does not show low angle.
A level full-body photograph with tall background alone fails.
A wide lens alone without upward projection fails.
A subject on a raised platform does not itself prove a low camera.
Numerical camera height cannot be measured from this image; only apparent position and projection are judged.
topic_criteria.evidence_units: visible regions and relationships at native size and reduced view

all_of: One adult fictional woman with reference-informed dark bob and face appearance.
Glass-roofed conservatory with visible iron ribs.
Right hand pressing a folded cloth against the vertical near edge of a narrow galvanized-metal potting bench.
Visible wet streak on that wiped edge.
Left hand cradling a separate spare towel bundle at waist.
Both boot soles contact a stone floor with staggered feet and upright torso.
Portrait full-body view includes contact, support and canopy together.

embodiment_pixel_checks: ownership of right cloth hand and left towel hand
both boot-floor contacts and stable balance
cloth-edge contact with distinct cloth and metal
